Area.evidence_source: The relationship with firearms and farming was commonly reported. There was an assumption that a firearm is the most likely suicide method because most farmers possess a firearm "and know how to kill things." Although not necessarily used on a regular basis, firearms were considered an occupational tool—"it's there if it is needed." An informant stated that "firearms were X's only possession." Another informant stated that the events leading to the farmer's death were indicative of the farmer's awareness of diminished physical capacity for the occupation, access to lethal means, and the functional role of a firearm. One farmer's gun license had been revoked due to a psychiatric diagnosis. Another had experienced the death of a child to suicide by firearm and subsequently, relinquished firearms during the national gun-buy-back scheme.
